newsitem.title: USA: Several factors behind Kansas crop data foul up.
newsitem.headline: Several factors behind Kansas crop data foul up.

text.p: A combination of human error and computer woes led to the release of incorrect data Monday on the condition of the Kansas wheat, corn and soybean crops, a U.S Agriculture Department aide said Tuesday.

Bill Dowdy, head of the field crops section in USDA's National Agricultural Statistics Service, said Kansas transmitted the wrong data to USDA, but discovered its error in time to send the correct information before the weekly Crop Progress report was released at 1600 EDT Monday.

By that time, NASS officials were grappling with "computer problems" that threatened to delay the report. Those were eventually fixed, but NASS officials forgot to change the crop progress tables to include the corrected Kansas data.
NASS issued revised tables at 900 EDT Tuesday, but decided against issuing a press release because it would have taken too long to get through the USDA approval proces.
Instead, NASS sent the corrected tables out over the Internet without informing news agencies.

NASS's motivation was to get the corrected information out as quickly as possible, Dowdy said. In the case of winter wheat, the revisions to Kansas condition were large enough to significantly change overall figures for the 19 key states.
Normal procedure is to wait until 1200 EDT Tuesday to release corrected data.
But the error was "a little bigger than we really felt comfortable with" and NASS officials wanted to get it out before futures market opened at 1030 EDT, Dowdy said.
